cohort: The study included 119 neonates who were admitted with suspected sepsis, divided into an infected group (N=40) and a control group (N=79).
finding: Serum pancreatic stone protein (PSP) concentrations were significantly higher in infected neonates compared to the control group at all time points (24, 72, and 168 hours after birth), confirming PSP as a valuable biomarker for predicting infected neonates.
